Each `application.yaml` is a complete Application, not a fragment: the generator copies its labels, annotations, finalizers and `spec` unchanged, and Renovate and the `Makefile` read it like any other manifest.

## Sync policy

Every Application, generated or not, carries the same `syncPolicy`: automated sync with `prune` and `selfHeal`, and a `retry` block of ten attempts with a backoff from 30s to 5m. That is the whole delivery contract:

- **A commit is live within one polling interval.** ArgoCD runs on a private address, so no GitHub webhook can reach it; the intervals are in [Platform → ArgoCD](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/#configuration>).
- **Drift is reverted.** A resource edited or deleted by hand is put back on the next reconcile, in the platform as much as in the workloads.
- **A failed sync retries itself.** ArgoCD never re-attempts a failed sync of the same revision unless the Application has a `retry` block, which is why every `application.yaml` carries one. The ten attempts span about forty minutes; after that the Application stays OutOfSync until its revision changes or it is synced by hand:

  ```bash
  argocd app sync <application>
  ```
- **Patching a generated Application's `spec` achieves nothing.** The next ApplicationSet reconcile copies the file back over it. That includes switching automated sync off: the only rollback is a revert commit — see [Rolling back a bad sync](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/troubleshooting/#rolling-back-a-bad-sync>).
- **One exception to `prune`, and one annotation.** `kube-vip` syncs with `prune: false`, because its objects are the only thing holding the API VIP; copy the `syncPolicy` from any other sibling. Elsewhere a resource whose deletion would take more than itself carries a per-resource `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false` instead: a Namespace (everything in it), an AppProject (every Application in it is orphaned), a CloudNativePG `Cluster` and the bucket its backups land in. A removed policy or manifest still prunes; the container it lived in stays.

## Bootstrap convergence

Nothing orders the Applications. On a fresh cluster the ApplicationSet generates all of them at once and they converge on their own: a sync that fails because a kind does not exist yet is retried once the chart that ships it has landed, and a resource that applies but cannot go Ready waits without failing anything. What each component waits for is in [Platform → Rollout order](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/#rollout-order>).

| While it is missing | The dependent Application | Resolves when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A CRD (`ServiceMonitor`, `HTTPRoute`, `ExternalSecret`, a Rook or CNPG kind) | fails its sync and retries | the chart shipping the CRD has synced |
| A `StorageClass` | is Progressing, its pods Pending | `rook-ceph-cluster` reports Ready |
| A working `ClusterSecretStore` | is Degraded on every `ExternalSecret` | OpenBao is unsealed and holds the key |
| A Gateway to attach to | is Progressing on every `HTTPRoute` | `gateway-api` holds its certificates |

Two placement rules keep this convergence short. **A resource lives with what it needs, not with what it configures:** the `ClusterSecretStore` is in `openbao`, not `external-secrets`, and cert-manager's issuers and certificates are their own `certificates` Application, so the controllers report Healthy on their own and the resources that wait for OpenBao are the ones that say so. **A resource that fails to apply for longer than the retry budget belongs elsewhere:** the budget covers a chart arriving minutes late, not a human arriving hours late.

### Bootstrap pauses at OpenBao

A fresh cluster looks stuck at OpenBao, and that is the design. OpenBao's pods report Ready while sealed, but the `ClusterSecretStore` beside it stays Degraded until OpenBao is initialised, unsealed and has the Kubernetes auth role, and with it every `ExternalSecret` in the platform. `make bao-init` clears that, and `make bao-unseal` after every later restart; `certificates` then waits for `make bao-secrets` to write the Route53 credentials, and the Gateways for the certificates. Nothing fails and nothing times out: every one of those resources applied cleanly and is waiting on status.

## Workloads live in a second repository

The applications the cluster exists to run are in [`JanWelker/homelab-apps`](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>), one directory per application; the `apps` ApplicationSet generates an Application from each `*/application.yaml` there. The split keeps a platform change with a cluster-wide blast radius apart from a workload change with a one-app one, and keeps the reusable half of the cluster in a repository that could build somebody else's.

The dependency runs one way: workloads reference the platform (the `apps-gateway`, the `rook-ceph-block` StorageClass, the `openbao` `ClusterSecretStore`, the CloudNativePG operator), and the platform references the workloads repository exactly once — the `repoURL` in `payload/workloads/applicationset.yaml`.

### What the split costs

- **Two repositories to clone**, and a change that spans both is two pull requests that cannot merge atomically; merge the platform half first.
- **The diff preview covers only this repository.** Both ApplicationSets carry `argocd-diff-preview/ignore` because the tool renders the repository it is given.
- **A workload can reference a platform resource that does not exist**, and nothing catches it until ArgoCD tries to sync.

### Workloads sync alongside the platform

The `apps` ApplicationSet ships inside the `workloads` Application, which the `platform` ApplicationSet generates like any component. That is why `payload/workloads/` is a sibling of `payload/platform/`, and why the `platform` ApplicationSet names it as a second generator path rather than a glob:

```yaml
        files:
          - path: payload/platform/*/application.yaml
          - path: payload/workloads/application.yaml
```

On a fresh cluster the workloads therefore start syncing before the platform under them is Healthy, and converge the same way it does: a workload `application.yaml` carries the same `retry` block, its `HTTPRoute` waits for the `apps-gateway`, its volumes for Rook, its secrets for OpenBao. Ordering *within* a workload uses resource-level sync waves — the CloudNativePG `Cluster` is in an earlier wave, and ArgoCD's built-in health check for `postgresql.cnpg.io/Cluster` waits for it before applying the application.

## Moving a resource to another Application

Moving a manifest between directories is not a move to ArgoCD: the old Application sees a tracked resource vanish and, with `prune: true`, deletes it; the new one recreates it, possibly seconds later. For a `ClusterSecretStore` that is an outage of every secret; for a child `Application` with the resources finalizer it deletes everything that Application deployed. A move takes two merges:

1. Annotate the resource where it is, and let that sync:

   ```yaml
   annotations:
     argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false
     argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: IgnoreExtraneous
   ```

   Both are read off the **live** object. `Prune=false` stops whichever Application prunes first; `IgnoreExtraneous` keeps the old Application Synced while it still sees the resource. 2. Move the file, keeping the annotations. The new Application takes over the tracking annotation.

The annotations can go once the second change has synced everywhere.

## Version pins

Each chart version is pinned once, in the `application.yaml` that owns the component; the node-level versions (Flatcar, Kubernetes, syslinux) are pinned once in `ansible/inventory.yaml`. The `Makefile` reads `targetRevision` out of the manifests for the bootstrap installs (`make install-cilium`, `make install-argo`), so what bootstrap installs is what ArgoCD then reconciles. kube-vip is the one double pin: `kube_vip_version` in the inventory for the bootstrap static pod, and the image in `payload/platform/kube-vip/daemonset.yaml` for what runs after the first sync. Renovate tracks all of them; its automerge policy is in [Maintenance](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/maintenance/index.md>).

# Known Limitations

Things this cluster does not do, collected so they are findable before they are discovered. None is a bug; each is an accepted tradeoff or work not yet done.

| Limitation | Consequence | Mitigation / plan | Where documented |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **The API endpoint address is fixed at `kubeadm init`** | `controlPlaneEndpoint` is the kube-vip VIP, and `kubeadm` bakes it into the API server certificates, every node's kubeconfig and the stored `ClusterConfiguration`; Cilium's `k8sServiceHost` names the same address. Moving the VIP to another address is therefore a certificate regeneration on every control-plane node and a kubeconfig rewrite on every node, not a config change that can be synced | Choose the address once, outside any DHCP range and apart from the LoadBalancer pools. The in-place procedure exists for the day it has to move; the next build [uses a name](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/#endpoint-name>) | [Choosing the address](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/#choosing-the-address>), [migrating in place](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/#in-place>) |
| **OpenBao needs an operator to unseal it** | Shamir seal, no auto-unseal: every restart (node reboot, Kured cycle, chart bump) leaves each replica sealed until the [threshold of key shares](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#at-a-glance>) is supplied. Sealed, no `ExternalSecret` resolves and cert-manager cannot renew. The cluster looks healthy; the consequence surfaces when a certificate expires | Check `bao status` after every reboot. Auto-unseal against a KMS or a second OpenBao would remove the step at the price of an external hard dependency; the key shares stay in the operator's hands on purpose | [Unsealing after a restart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#unsealing-after-a-restart>), [after any node reboot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/#after-any-node-reboot-unseal-openbao>) |
| **Alerting reaches one mailbox** | One receiver, one mailbox, one SMTP provider, unmonitored. If mail is rejected or the password expires, alerts stop silently; `Watchdog` proves the pipeline only as far as Alertmanager | A second receiver on a different transport. Meanwhile, run the routine health check | [Alerting](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/#alerting>), [routine health check](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/#routine-health-check>) |
| **Backups do not leave the cluster** | Velero and the etcd snapshot CronJob write to the Ceph object store the cluster runs on: protection against a deleted PVC or a bad `prune`, none against losing the cluster | RGW bucket replication or a second Velero `BackupStorageLocation`; neither is configured. Until then disaster recovery is Git plus the OpenBao unseal keys | [Backups &amp; Recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md>) |
| **Automatic updates stop at patch releases** | Sysupdate is pinned to the Kubernetes major.minor in `ansible/inventory.yaml`; Kured drains and reboots one node at a time to apply what is staged, and refuses while Ceph or etcd is unhealthy. A minor Kubernetes upgrade is manual: change the inventory, push the sysupdate config to running nodes, run `kubeadm upgrade`. Kured blocks only on the alerts named in its config; anything outside that list does not stop a reboot | By design | [Nodes are pinned to a minor series](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/#nodes-are-pinned-to-a-minor-series>), [upgrading a minor deliberately](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/upgrades/#upgrading-a-minor-version-deliberately>), [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) |
| **The `infra` AppProject is permissive** | The network policies are enforced, but the `infra` AppProject allows every kind in every namespace, so a platform `application.yaml` can deploy anything anywhere | Narrow the projects | [Security Posture](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/security/#authorization>) |
| **Reprovisioning needs the boot server on the segment** | Rebuilding a node means `make serve` on a machine on the nodes' L2 segment, the external DHCP pointing at it, `make reinstall LIMIT=<node>`, and a power cycle. There is no remote rebuild, and the deployment host is not part of the cluster | Only *re*provisioning: Flatcar is installed to disk, so a running node reboots, updates and rejoins with the boot server off | [Boot &amp; Bootstrap Process](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/#every-boot-after-the-first>) |
| **The object store survives one host down, no more** | During every Kured reboot the RGW data pool, which holds the Velero backups and Loki chunks, has no redundancy left, while `rbd-pool` still has some | Accepted, no migration: Ceph cannot change the erasure profile of an existing pool, so changing it means a new pool and moving every bucket | [Object storage](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/#object-storage>) |
| **Single region, site and rack** | No failure domain larger than a node. Ceph replicates across nodes on one power feed; a site-level event takes everything | The honest limit of a homelab | — |

# Security Posture

This is a homelab on a private network, and several deliberate shortcuts follow from that. They are listed so that someone reading the manifests can tell a decision from an oversight.

## Assumed trust boundary

The cluster assumes a **trusted L2 network segment**: anything with a port on it is treated as friendly. There is no VPN requirement and no mutual TLS between components; inside the cluster, the default-deny network policies in [Authorization](<#authorization>) are the segmentation.

The published hostnames are a partial exception. Certificates come from Let's Encrypt through a DNS-01 challenge against a public zone, so `argo.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` and its siblings are publicly resolvable and appear in Certificate Transparency logs, even though they point at RFC1918 addresses. Plan names accordingly.

## Provisioning

Provisioning is the least protected phase, by design: it has to work before any of the cluster's own security exists.

| Property | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Ignition configs are served unauthenticated over HTTP | Anything on the segment can fetch `http://<boot-server>:8000/ignition-<host>.json` while the boot server is running |
| Those configs embed join credentials | The bootstrap `token`, and on control-plane nodes the `certificateKey`, together enough to join a new control-plane node. Only the init host has them in its kubeadm config; the others get a `0600` environment file that `bootstrap-k8s.service` names by variable and deletes after a successful join, so `systemctl cat` and `systemctl show` reveal nothing |
| The control-plane configs embed the etcd encryption key | `/etc/kubernetes/enc/encryption-config.yaml` is inlined with the key that encrypts every Secret at rest. It has no TTL: anyone who fetched a control-plane config while the boot server was up can read Secrets out of any etcd backup, for the life of the cluster |
| Nodes join with `--discovery-token-unsafe-skip-ca-verification` | A joining node does not verify the API server's CA |
| Sysext updates set `Verify=false` | On first boot Ignition checks each image against the sha256 the boot server was given, so a substituted image fails. Later sysupdate downloads travel over HTTPS with signature verification off. The transfer config that names their source is inlined from a template in Git, not fetched |
| The PXE kernel, initrd and bootloader are signature-checked | `make download` takes their sums only from a clearsigned file that `gpgv` verifies against a pinned primary key fingerprint: Flatcar's image signing key for `.DIGESTS.asc`, the kernel.org checksum autosigner for syslinux's `sha256sums.asc` |
| The OS image is signature-checked | `flatcar-install` is given `-b`/`-V`, so the node downloads the image and its detached signature and checks both against Flatcar's key before writing anything |

The mitigation is time: `make serve` is a foreground command, the bootstrap token and the certificate key expire (the windows are in [Switching back to local boot](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/#switching-back-to-local-boot>)), and `make config` re-arms both only for those windows. The encryption key has no clock, which is why the HTTP server listens only on `boot_server_ip`, serves files by name and lists nothing. TFTP listens on every interface, because macOS lets an unprivileged process bind port 69 only there, and refuses every write request, so nobody can plant a boot menu. **Stop the boot server when provisioning is finished.** Flatcar is installed to disk, so nothing needs it after a build — see [Every boot after the first](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/boot-process/#every-boot-after-the-first>).

`output/credentials/` holds the generated bootstrap token and certificate key in plaintext. The directory is `0700`, the Ignition configs in `output/http` are `0600`, and `output/` is gitignored. The values are reused across `make config` runs, because a node whose join window passed retries with the values on its disk once `make config` has re-armed them ([Adding a node](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/#adding-a-node>)). Delete them to force new ones. The installer keeps its copy of the node config `0600` in RAM; `flatcar-install` carries that mode to the OEM partition.

## Node hardening

`ansible/templates/kubeadm.yaml.j2` and `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2` carry the settings below. They land at provisioning time and change only on `make reinstall`.

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `proxy.disabled: true` | Cilium replaces `kube-proxy`. The field lands in the `kubeadm-config` ConfigMap that `kubeadm upgrade apply` reads; a `skipPhases` on init alone leaves `proxy: {}` stored, and every upgrade puts `kube-proxy` back beside Cilium |
| `--kubelet-certificate-authority` | The API server verifies the kubelet's serving certificate for exec, logs, attach and port-forward, the calls that carry command output. It can, because `serverTLSBootstrap` makes the kubelet request its certificate from the cluster CA and [kubelet-csr-approver](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md>) approves the CSR; metrics-server verifies the same certificates |
| `--admission-control-config-file` | A [Pod Security default](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#pod-security-admission>) for namespaces without labels, so a namespace nobody labelled is `baseline`, not `privileged` |
| `--profiling=false` on the API server, controller-manager and scheduler | `/debug/pprof` exposes internals to any token with the right RBAC and helps nothing here; CIS asks for it off |
| Metrics listeners on the node address | etcd's plain-HTTP metrics and the controller-manager and scheduler bind the node's own address, where Prometheus scrapes them, instead of every interface. The address differs per node, so it comes from per-node JSON patches in `/etc/kubernetes/patches` rather than the cluster-wide `ClusterConfiguration`; the patches also move the probes, and etcd keeps `127.0.0.1` for its own |
| `DenyServiceExternalIPs` | `spec.externalIPs` lets whoever can create a Service claim traffic to any address on every node, with no ownership check. Nothing here uses it: LoadBalancer addresses come from Cilium's pools. `NodeRestriction` is repeated because the flag replaces kubeadm's default list |
| `--tls-cipher-suites` and `--tls-min-version`, `tlsCipherSuites` and `tlsMinVersion` | Go's defaults still include CBC and 3DES suites; the list keeps AEAD suites on ECDHE, which every client here speaks (kubectl, the controllers and the kubelets are all Go). TLS 1.3 ignores the list; the floor stops a downgrade to 1.0 or 1.1. The kubelet's own listener on port 10250 gets the same list and floor, since the API server, metrics-server and Prometheus are its only clients |
| `shutdownGracePeriod` and `shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods` | The kubelet holds a systemd inhibitor lock, so a `systemctl reboot` without the [documented drain](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/nodes/#rebooting-a-node>), or an ACPI power-off, waits while pods get their SIGTERM window instead of killing them mid-write; the second value is the tail of the first that only critical pods may use. CloudNativePG primaries and Ceph OSDs are the ones that notice |
| `protectKernelDefaults: true` | The kubelet no longer rewrites `vm.overcommit_memory`, `vm.panic_on_oom`, `kernel.panic` and `kernel.panic_on_oops` at start and refuses to start unless they are already right. `/etc/sysctl.d/k8s.conf` in the node config sets them, and the two travel together: without the drop-in a fresh node comes up at the kernel defaults, the kubelet exits and the node never joins, which shows at the next `make reinstall`, not on merge |
| `kernel.panic` with `kernel.panic_on_oops` | An oops reboots the node after a few seconds instead of leaving it wedged, so Ceph and etcd start recovering without a hand power-cycle |
| `podPidsLimit` | Bounds the PIDs one pod can hold, so a process that stops reaping its children cannot exhaust the node's PID space and take the kubelet with it. Well above anything running here, well below `kernel.pid_max` |
| `systemReserved`, `kubeReserved` and `evictionHard` memory | The reservations cap `kubepods.slice` below the node's RAM, so a pod that grows, the API server included, is OOM-killed inside its own cgroup instead of starving systemd-networkd, sshd and the kubelet. The eviction threshold makes the kubelet evict before the kernel has to act. A running node needs the same values in the `kubelet-config` ConfigMap, or `kubeadm upgrade node` reverts them |
| `/etc/tmpfiles.d/kubernetes-cis.conf` | kubeadm writes its files 0644 and Cilium creates the CNI directory 0755; CIS wants 0600 and 0700. systemd-tmpfiles applies the modes at boot and a kubelet `ExecStartPre` re-applies them before every start, when kubeadm has just rewritten them. See [Triage 2026-09-20](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/triage-2026-09-20/#infra-the-nodes>) |
| `systemd-sysupdate-reboot.timer` masked | Flatcar ships a vendor symlink that runs it despite a disabled preset. It would reboot on its own schedule, behind [Kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) and without a drain, and it fails every run anyway: it acts on the default sysupdate component, which holds only `noop.conf` |
| `noop.conf` in `/etc/sysupdate.d/` | The unsuffixed directory is the default component that `systemd-sysupdate.service` acts on; the no-op transfer keeps that run from failing while the real transfer sits in the `kubernetes.d` component |

## Secrets

Secrets live in [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) and reach workloads as native Kubernetes `Secret` objects through the [External Secrets Operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md>). Nothing sensitive is committed to Git.

- OpenBao is sealed with Shamir and [unsealed by hand](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#unsealing-after-a-restart>), so the 5 key shares are the root of trust for every other secret; losing all of them loses everything, and nothing outside the cluster holds a copy.
- No root token is kept: `make bao-init` revokes it once it has created the [operator login](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#operator-credential>), and one is generated from the shares when needed. The operator login reads and writes every KV path, so `output/credentials/` is as sensitive as before, but it cannot change policies or auth methods.
- A workload's namespace reaches only `kv/<namespace>/` in OpenBao; the platform's store refuses every other namespace — see [Kubernetes auth](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#kubernetes-auth>).
- A Kubernetes `Secret` is base64, not encryption. Anyone with `get secrets` in a namespace can read what ESO materialised there. Encryption at rest protects the bytes in etcd, not the API.
- Velero's resource backups hold every `Secret` as plain JSON in the `velero` bucket, so its keys and RGW bypass encryption at rest; only the volume data is encrypted — see [Velero](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/#repository-password>).

### Encryption at rest

The API server encrypts `secrets` with `secretbox` before they reach etcd (`ansible/templates/kubeadm.yaml.j2`; the key file in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`). Without it an etcd backup, a stolen disk, or read access to `/var/lib/etcd` yields every credential the cluster holds.

| Property | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Provider | `secretbox`, with `identity` listed after it |
| Key | 32 random letters and digits (about 190 bits), generated once by `make config` into `output/credentials/encryption_key` and base64-encoded into the config as the `secretbox` key |
| Scope | `secrets` only; ConfigMaps and other resources are unencrypted |
| Distribution | The same key on every control-plane node, written by Ignition to `/etc/kubernetes/enc/encryption-config.yaml` (mode `0600`) |

With `identity` last, new writes are encrypted and Secrets written before it was enabled stay readable but are not rewritten. To encrypt what already exists, once the API servers have restarted:

```bash
kubectl get secrets -A -o json | kubectl replace -f -
```

The key lives in `output/credentials/` beside the kubeadm token and certificate key — that directory is what decrypts etcd. The API servers reload the config file on change (`encryption-provider-config-automatic-reload`), so rotating it is a file edit and a rewrite of every Secret, by hand — see [Encryption Key Rotation](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/encryption-key-rotation/index.md>). A KMS provider would remove the key file at the cost of a dependency the cluster must reach before it can serve Secrets.

## Runtime

[Tetragon](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md>) records every exec in every pod and alerts when anything but the control plane reads the cluster's key material. It is detection, not prevention: nothing is killed, and a policy that fails to load on a new kernel watches nothing until its alert fires.

## Audit logging

The API server records who did what, to which object, and whether it was allowed; the `audit` half of the Pod Security Admission labels has nowhere to go without it. Policy, retention and queries are in [Audit Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/audit-logging/index.md>).

## Authorization

**AppProjects constrain the workloads, not the platform.** `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml` defines them. `infra` allows `sourceRepos: "*"` and every group and kind in every namespace: it is this repository deploying this repository, and a restriction there guards against nothing the PR review does not. `system` is confined to the `argocd` namespace. `apps` has the boundary to draw, because its Applications come from a second repository with a lighter review: it accepts only the workloads repository and the chart repositories the workloads use, may not write into any platform namespace (`authentik` excepted, where an admission policy narrows it to the workload's own blueprint ConfigMap), and at cluster scope may create nothing but namespaces, never at the `privileged` Pod Security level — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#admission-policies>).

**Every platform namespace is default-deny in both directions**, one `CiliumNetworkPolicy` file per namespace plus the cluster-wide rules, and Cilium enforces them: `policyAuditMode` is off, so a flow no rule allows is dropped — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>) and [Rollout](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#rollout>).

**Pod Security Admission is on, but mostly auditing.** Every platform namespace carries `enforce` at the level it demonstrably needs and `warn`/`audit` at a stricter one, so violations are visible without breaking what runs: measure first, enforce second.

**Image references are checked at admission.** An untagged or `latest` image is refused; a registry outside the allowlist is recorded and warned about but admitted. Signatures are not verified: few of the upstreams sign, so a verifier would exempt nearly everything. See [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#admission-policies>).

**Both Gateways admit routes from every namespace** (`allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: All`). Any namespace can attach an `HTTPRoute` to either Gateway and claim a hostname inside its listener's pattern — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/#configuration>).

## Exposed interfaces

Every platform UI on the infra gateway, and Flowscape and the Extractor admin UI on the apps gateway, is behind [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>), and only accounts in `infra-users` get past it. The wollbi editors also have Authentik accounts, so being logged in is not enough. The last two rows are not behind Authentik:

| Service | Authentication | Group required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | Authentik OIDC; local admin disabled. The server runs with `--insecure` because TLS terminates at the Gateway | `infra-users`, then `argocd-admins` or `argocd-viewers` for any access |
| Grafana | Authentik OIDC; login form disabled | `infra-users`; refused without `grafana-admins`, `grafana-editors` or direct `infra-users` |
| Hubble UI | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Rook dashboard | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Prometheus | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Alertmanager | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| Flowscape, Extractor admin UI | Authentik proxy outpost | `infra-users` |
| OpenBao UI | Token or configured auth method — not behind Authentik | — |
| Agent SSH, `*.ssh.wlkr.ch` | The `ssh` TLS-passthrough listener on `apps-gateway`, which external-dns publishes on the public address. Nothing in front authenticates it: `sshd` in each agent pod admits the user `agent` with public keys only — see [SSH listener](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/#ssh-listener>) and the workloads repository's [Claude agents](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps/blob/main/docs/claude-agents.md>) page | — |

The groups and how they nest are in [Groups and roles](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#groups-and-roles>).

Authentik is therefore a dependency of reaching any of them; the break-glass paths are in [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#when-authentik-is-down>). OpenBao is left out deliberately: it holds Authentik's own database password, so putting it behind Authentik would be a loop.

## What would tighten this up

Roughly in order of value against effort:

1. Narrow `sourceRepos` on the AppProjects to this repository and the Helm repositories actually in use.
2. Restrict `allowedRoutes` on `infra-gateway` to the platform namespaces, and promote the registry allowlist to `Deny`.
3. Add a second Alertmanager receiver on a different transport, so a failure of the mail path is not itself unmonitored.
4. Move etcd encryption to a KMS provider, removing the static `encryption_key` in `output/credentials/`.
5. Get the backups out of the cluster: Velero and the etcd snapshots write to the Ceph object store they are backing up.

See [Known Limitations](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/limitations/index.md>) for the operational counterparts.

# Platform

# Platform

The core infrastructure components that run the cluster, all managed by ArgoCD. Every one of them exists because bare metal does not come with the thing a cloud provider would have handed you: no load balancer, no managed certificates, no block storage API, no identity provider, no backup service.

## Components

One row per directory under `payload/platform/`, with the Application name where it differs from the directory — that is the name `kubectl -n argocd get applications` shows — and the namespace it lands in.

| Component | Namespace | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| alloy | `logging` | Grafana Alloy, the log shipper — see [Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) |
| arc-controller | `arc-systems` | The Actions Runner Controller — see [GitHub runners](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/github-runners/index.md>) |
| [arc-runners](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/github-runners/index.md>) | `arc-runners`, `arc-jobs` | Self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, one scale set per repository |
| [argocd](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md>) | `argocd` | ArgoCD itself and the `platform` ApplicationSet |
| argocd-config | `argocd` | The `ExternalSecret` for ArgoCD's OIDC client, and its Grafana dashboard; see [ArgoCD](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/index.md>) |
| argocd-projects | `argocd` | The AppProjects; see [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#structure>) |
| [authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) | `authentik` | Single sign-on for every platform UI |
| backup | `backup` | Velero's buckets, the `VolumeSnapshotClass` and an etcd snapshot CronJob — see [Backups &amp; Recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md>) |
| [cert-manager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cert-manager/index.md>) | `cert-manager` | The cert-manager chart |
| certificates | `cert-manager` | The Let's Encrypt issuers and the Gateway wildcard certificates — see [cert-manager](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cert-manager/index.md>) |
| [cilium](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cilium/index.md>) | `kube-system` | CNI, `kube-proxy` replacement, Gateway API, LoadBalancer addresses, WireGuard, Hubble |
| [cloudnative-pg](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md>) | `cnpg-system` | The PostgreSQL operator every workload database runs on |
| [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) | `descheduler` | Evicts pods a drain or reboot left piled on the surviving nodes |
| [external-dns](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-dns/index.md>) | `external-dns` | Publishes Route53 records from HTTPRoutes |
| [external-secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md>) | `external-secrets` | Bridges OpenBao to native Kubernetes Secrets |
| [gateway-api](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) | `kube-system` | The two Gateways and the HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect |
| gateway-api-crds | `kube-system` | The Gateway API CRDs — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) |
| kube-vip | `kube-system` | Holds the control-plane VIP; adopts the static pod Ignition bootstraps — see [Control Plane VIP](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/control-plane-vip/index.md>) |
| kubelet-csr-approver | `kubelet-csr-approver` | Approves `kubelet-serving` CSRs against the inventory — see [Metrics Server](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/#verifying-the-kubelet-instead-of-trusting-it>) |
| [kured](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/kured/index.md>) | `kured` | Drains and reboots nodes to apply staged OS and Kubernetes updates |
| [logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) | `logging` | Loki's bucket, rules, dashboards and Grafana datasource |
| loki | `logging` | The Loki chart — see [Logging](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/logging/index.md>) |
| [metrics-server](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/metrics-server/index.md>) | `kube-system` | The `metrics.k8s.io` API behind `kubectl top` and every HPA |
| monitoring, Application `kube-prometheus-stack` | `monitoring`, `node-exporter` | Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, kube-state-metrics; node-exporter alone in `node-exporter` — see [Monitoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/index.md>) |
| [openbao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) | `openbao` | Cluster-wide secret store |
| prometheus-operator-crds | `monitoring` | The Prometheus operator CRDs, separate so every chart that ships a `ServiceMonitor` can sync — see [Monitoring](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/monitoring/#crds>) |
| [rook-ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) | `rook-ceph` | The CSI driver, dashboards and HTTPRoute |
| rook-ceph-cluster | `rook-ceph` | The `CephCluster`, pools and storage classes — see [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) |
| rook-ceph-operator | `rook-ceph` | The Rook operator chart — see [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) |
| security | `kube-system` | Pod Security Admission levels, the network policies and image admission policies — see [Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/index.md>) |
| snapshot-controller | `backup` | The CSI snapshot controller Velero's volume snapshots need — see [Backups &amp; Recovery](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/operations/backups/index.md>) |
| [tetragon](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/tetragon/index.md>) | `kube-system` | Runtime detection: execs, credential changes and sensitive file reads from the kernel |
| [trivy-operator](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/trivy-operator/index.md>) | `trivy-system` | Vulnerability, misconfiguration, secret, RBAC and CIS scanning, every finding a CRD |
| [velero](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/velero/index.md>) | `backup` | Volume and resource backups to the Ceph object store |

Across the platform, memory limits are set at roughly 2.5x the measured peak working set and requests at steady state; CPU is requested but never limited. The control-plane static pods get their memory requests through the kubeadm patches in `ansible/templates/butane_node_config.yaml.j2`, applied at `kubeadm init`, `join` and `upgrade`, so a running node picks them up at its next reinstall; they carry no limits, because a limit on the API server or etcd would OOM-kill the control plane and 2.5x their peak exceeds the node. CoreDNS is kubeadm's too: the same directory holds a patch spreading its replicas one per node, which kubeadm applies at `init` and `upgrade apply` only, and its PodDisruptionBudget sits in the `security` component because nothing else owns a CoreDNS manifest.

Components the cluster cannot run without — the CNI and API VIP, the admission webhooks, the secret and certificate chain, the CSR approver, the storage daemons and the node security agents — carry a `system-*` priority class, so under node pressure the kubelet evicts workloads first: `system-node-critical` for the DaemonSets a node needs, `system-cluster-critical` for the rest.

## Traffic Flow

```
flowchart LR
    Client([Client]) --> LB[Cilium LoadBalancer]
    LB --> GW[Gateway API]

    subgraph Cluster
        GW -->|HTTPRoute| Svc[Service]
        Svc --> Pod[App Pod]
    end

    style Client fill:#f9f,stroke:#333
```

Four hops, and Cilium is three of them. When a hostname stops answering, ask which hop stopped, in this order: does the Gateway still hold its LoadBalancer IP, does the `HTTPRoute` still say `Accepted`, does the Service still have endpoints.

## HTTPRoute Locations

Routes sit with the component they expose, as a manifest where the component is plain YAML and as chart values where the chart renders its own:

| Service | URL | Route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | `argo.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.httproute` in `payload/argocd/values.yaml` |
| ArgoCD CLI (gRPC) | `argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.grpcroute` in `payload/argocd/values.yaml` |
| Authentik | `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/authentik/httproute.yaml` |
| Prometheus | `prometheus.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/monitoring/httproute.yaml` |
| Alertmanager | `alertmanager.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/monitoring/httproute.yaml` |
| Grafana | `monitoring.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `grafana.route.main` in `payload/platform/monitoring/application.yaml` |
| Hubble | `hubble.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/cilium/httproute.yaml` |
| OpenBao UI | `vault.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `server.gateway.httpRoute` in `payload/platform/openbao/application.yaml` |
| Rook dashboard | `rook.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/rook-ceph/httproute.yaml` |
| Ceph object store | `s3.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `payload/platform/rook-ceph/httproute.yaml` |
| Home Assistant | `home.k8s.wlkr.ch` | `home-assistant/httproute.yaml` in [homelab-apps](<https://github.com/JanWelker/homelab-apps>) |

## Deployment

```bash
make bootstrap  # Gateway API CRDs + Cilium, ArgoCD, then the handover
```

After that the `argocd` Application syncs the `platform` ApplicationSet, which generates one Application per `payload/platform/*/application.yaml` plus the `workloads` Application that deploys the `apps` ApplicationSet for the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>). Each component directory holds exactly one `application.yaml`; everything else in it is what that Application deploys. [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md>) has the structure and the sync policy.

## Replica placement

Two replicas on one node are not redundancy. Every chart's default is a single `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` anti-affinity term — one weight among the scheduler's scores, and on a cluster of one 16 GB worker against two 8 GB ones, free memory outscores it. So every component with more than one replica carries an explicit rule:

| Rule | When |
| --- | --- |
| `topologySpreadConstraints`, `maxSkew: 1`, `whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway` | the component runs on the three workers only, where a hard rule would leave a replica `Pending` through a Kured drain |
| `podAntiAffinity` `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` | the component tolerates the control planes, so every node is a candidate and a drain always leaves room — or its chart exposes no spread constraint |

Constraints carry `nodeTaintsPolicy: Honor`, so the skew is measured over the nodes the pod can reach rather than over the tainted control planes. Where a component carries a PodDisruptionBudget it says `maxUnavailable: 1`, so a drain or the [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) evicts one replica at a time; `maxUnavailable` rather than `minAvailable`, so a component scaled down to one replica never blocks a drain. The CloudNativePG operator runs two replicas with no budget. Placement is scored once, at scheduling time: pods already sharing a node stay there until something restarts them, and the [descheduler](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/descheduler/index.md>) moves them back only if its evictor is allowed to touch them.

## Rollout order

Nothing enforces an order: every Application syncs as soon as it exists and converges by retry and health, as [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#bootstrap-convergence>) explains. This is the order a fresh cluster settles in, and what each layer is waiting for while it is not yet Healthy.

| Layer | Applications | Waits for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Projects and CRDs | `argocd-projects`, `gateway-api-crds`, `prometheus-operator-crds` | — |
| Network | `cilium`, `kube-vip` | the Gateway API CRDs Cilium's operator reads at startup |
| Controllers | `arc-controller`, `cert-manager`, `cloudnative-pg`, `external-secrets`, `kubelet-csr-approver`, `rook-ceph-operator`, `snapshot-controller` | a network; each brings its own CRDs |
| Storage | `rook-ceph`, `rook-ceph-cluster` | the Rook operator and its CRDs |
| Secrets | `openbao` | `rook-ceph-block` for its volumes, then an operator — see [Bootstrap pauses at OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#bootstrap-pauses-at-openbao>) |
| Certificates | `certificates`, `external-dns` | a working `ClusterSecretStore` and the Route53 credentials in OpenBao |
| Ingress | `gateway-api` | the wildcard certificates the Gateways terminate TLS with |
| Services | `arc-runners`, `argocd-config`, `authentik`, `backup`, `kube-prometheus-stack`, `logging`, `metrics-server` | secrets, storage, the Gateways, and approved kubelet certificates |
| Backends | `loki`, `velero` | the buckets `logging` and `backup` claim |
| Agents | `alloy`, `tetragon` | Loki, so the collector has somewhere to ship |
| Policy | `descheduler`, `kured`, `security`, `trivy-operator` | namespaces to label, a Prometheus to scrape and metrics-server for node usage; kured reboots only on a staged update, never on a fresh install |
| Workloads | `workloads` | nothing on its own; the workloads it generates wait for the platform resources they reference — see the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>) |

Why the `ClusterSecretStore` sits with OpenBao and the issuers are their own Application is in [Bootstrap convergence](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#bootstrap-convergence>).

# ArgoCD

ArgoCD is the delivery layer: everything in `payload/` and in the workloads repository reaches the cluster through it. How the Applications are generated and synced is in [GitOps Strategy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/index.md>); this page covers the chart values and the supporting resources around ArgoCD itself.

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace | `argocd` |
| Depends on | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) for the OIDC client secret, [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/index.md>) for its route, [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) for every login |
| If it is down | Nothing syncs. Running workloads are unaffected |
| Health check | `kubectl -n argocd get applications` → every one `Synced` and `Healthy` |
| Files | `payload/argocd/` (Application, `platform` ApplicationSet, `values.yaml`), `payload/platform/argocd-config/` (OIDC `ExternalSecret`, Grafana dashboard), `payload/platform/argocd-projects/` (AppProjects) |

## Configuration

The parts of `payload/argocd/values.yaml` that are not self-explanatory:

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `redis-ha.haproxy` `maxSurge: 0` | Three replicas with hard per-host anti-affinity on three schedulable nodes. The default surges a fourth pod with nowhere to land and wedges every rollout; retiring first frees the node |
| `redis-ha.image.tag`, `redis-ha.haproxy.image.tag` | Both run ahead of the chart, whose exact patch tags stop being rebuilt once the next one lands and so miss base-image security fixes. Renovate carries them forward; each bare `tag:` must be listed under the `pinDigests: false` rule in `renovate.json` |
| Memory limits, no CPU limits | A CPU limit throttles even on an idle node; memory is not compressible. Sizing is in [Platform](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/index.md>) |
| `metrics.enabled` on four components | Creates the `<component>-metrics` Services whose names are the `job` label the vendored dashboard filters on. The ServiceMonitors render only once the Prometheus operator CRDs exist, so `make install-argo` still works first |
| `configs.params` `server.insecure: true` | TLS terminates at the Gateway. The chart reads this parameter, not `extraArgs`, to point its route at the plaintext port |
| `server.httproute` | The chart renders the `HTTPRoute` to `argocd-server`, so it is not a file of its own; the response-header filters are the same every UI route carries — see [Gateway API](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/#usage>) |
| `resource.customizations` for `HTTPRoute` | The API server defaults `group`, `kind`, `weight` and a catch-all `matches` onto every route; without the ignore list each one is permanently OutOfSync. Only the catch-all value is ignored, so a changed path still syncs |
| `dex.enabled: false` | `oidc.config` talks to [Authentik](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/index.md>) directly, so the chart's bundled Dex would be a second login service with nothing behind it; the redirect URI is the server's own `/auth/callback` either way |
| `admin.enabled: "false"` | With SSO in front, a shared admin password would bypass it with no audit trail |
| `resource.customizations.health.argoproj.io_Application` | Restores health assessment for `Application` resources, dropped in ArgoCD 1.8, so `argocd` reports the health of the ApplicationSet rather than a permanent Healthy |
| `policy.default: ""` | An authenticated user with no matching Authentik group gets no access, not read-only-everything |
| `timeout.reconciliation` and the ApplicationSets' `requeueAfterSeconds` | ArgoCD listens on a private address, so GitHub's webhook cannot reach it and a commit waits for the next poll. The two run separately: the first refreshes Applications, the second re-reads the generator paths. The repo-server caches a revision for the first, so it must not exceed the second or a new commit's files stay invisible to the generator until the cache expires |

The OIDC client ID and secret come from `kv/authentik/config`, the same OpenBao path Authentik's blueprint reads. `argocd-cm` refers to them as `$argocd-oidc:client-id`; ArgoCD resolves a `$name:key` reference only against a Secret labelled `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: argocd`, which the `ExternalSecret` template sets.

The Grafana dashboard in `grafana-dashboards.yaml` is upstream's `examples/dashboard.json`, unmodified, at the ArgoCD version the chart deploys. Renovate does not see it: re-copy it when ArgoCD moves a minor version.

## Usage

### Projects

The `apps` project lists the repositories its Applications may pull from in `payload/platform/argocd-projects/projects.yaml`. An OCI Helm chart is listed and referenced **without** the `oci://` scheme (`ghcr.io/janwelker/charts` as `sourceRepos` entry and as the Application's `repoURL`, with `chart:` naming the chart): Argo CD compares the two strings after normalising, and treats a `repoURL` with no scheme as OCI, so a public registry needs no repository Secret and no `enableOCI`. The `default` project Argo CD creates on install is declared in the same file with empty lists: it cannot be deleted, so an Application that names no project lands there and must be able to do nothing.

### Agent account

The `claude` account is the in-cluster Claude Code agents' API identity. It may read everything `role:readonly` reads, `argocd app get --refresh` included, and nothing else: the sessions investigate and open pull requests, and every Application syncs itself. It has `apiKey` only, so it cannot log in. One token serves every session with `argocd.enabled`, so its expiry is what bounds a leak from any of them.

The token expires after 90 days: that caps a leak at a quarter, and rotating is a few commands with no restart. An expired token fails every agent `argocd` call until the next one is stored. To rotate:

1. Generate the token, logged in through Authentik:

   ```bash
   argocd account generate-token --account claude --expires-in 90d
   ```
2. Store it with `make bao-secrets`, at `kv/claude-agents/argocd` (`token`).
3. Pull it into the sessions now instead of at the next `refreshInterval`. The chart mounts the token as a file that the `argocd` wrapper reads on every call, so no pod restarts; only a shell opened earlier keeps the old token in its environment:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n claude-agents annotate externalsecret claude-<session>-argocd force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite
   ```
4. Revoke the previous token. `argocd account get --account claude` lists the token IDs with their expiry dates:

   ```bash
   argocd account delete-token --account claude <id>
   ```

The agents reach Argo CD on 443 through the CLI host from [CLI access](<#cli-access>), which resolves to `infra-gateway`'s own address. The caller's policy has to admit both legs, as for any name the Gateway serves ([Security Policies](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#network-policies>)):

| Leg | Admitted by |
| --- | --- |
| Agent pod to the Gateway address | A name rule for the CLI host: the datapath classifies the Gateway's address as `world`, not `ingress` |
| The Gateway's Envoy to `argocd-server` | An egress rule to the `argocd-server` pod itself. Envoy checks the caller's egress policy again against the pod it picked and answers `403 Access denied` when no rule matches, audit mode or not. The server's own policy already admits the `ingress` entity |

The `homelab` session's policy in the workloads repository carries both. The chart's own policy has only the name rule ([claude-agent\#3](<https://github.com/JanWelker/claude-agent/issues/3>)), so any other session with `argocd.enabled` gets a 403 on every call.

### CLI access

The `argocd` CLI talks gRPC, which the browser route cannot carry: Cilium's Gateway translates gRPC-web into native gRPC, and native gRPC needs an HTTP/2 backend, which the plain `http` port is not. The chart therefore adds an `h2c` port (`http2`, 81) and a `GRPCRoute` on `argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch`, a hostname of its own so the browser route stays as it is.

The Gateway offers no ALPN, and gRPC clients refuse TLS without it, so the CLI needs ALPN enforcement off:

```bash
export GRPC_ENFORCE_ALPN_ENABLED=false
argocd login argo-grpc.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch --sso --grpc-web
```

## Health check

```bash
kubectl -n argocd get applications
```

Every Application should be `Synced` and `Healthy`. One that stays `OutOfSync` has exhausted its retries and waits for a hand sync — see [Sync policy](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#sync-policy>).

## Pitfalls

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The local admin is disabled; Authentik is the login**
>
> With Authentik down there is no way into the UI. The break-glass path is a pull request that re-enables `admin.enabled`, since selfHeal reverts a `kubectl patch`; the steps are in [When Authentik is down](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/authentik/#when-authentik-is-down>).

## Recovery

### Reinstalling the chart

ArgoCD manages ArgoCD, and the ApplicationSet that deploys the cluster sits inside that same Application. When a broken ArgoCD config has been synced by ArgoCD, `make install-argo` reinstalls the chart from the deployment host, and `kubectl apply -f payload/argocd/applicationset-platform.yaml` re-applies the rollout itself.

# Authentik

[Authentik](<https://goauthentik.io/>) is the cluster's identity provider. Every platform UI sits behind one login instead of a chart-default password each — and Hubble UI, which ships no authentication at all, would otherwise publish every network flow in the cluster to anyone who could reach the hostname.

| Service | Authentication |
| --- | --- |
| ArgoCD | OIDC, local admin **disabled** |
| Grafana | OIDC, login form disabled |
| Home Assistant | Proxy outpost **in front of** its own login — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| Umami | Proxy outpost **in front of** its own login; the tracker paths pass through — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| Rook dashboard, Hubble UI, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Flowscape, Extractor admin UI | Proxy outpost |
| Wollbi-Fescht, Wollbi Adventsfenster | Proxy outpost on the admin paths, with no `infra-users` binding, see [Groups and roles](<#groups-and-roles>) |

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace | `authentik` |
| Depends on | [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) for its OIDC client secrets, [CloudNativePG](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/index.md>) for the database, [Rook-Ceph](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/rook-ceph/index.md>) under it |
| If it is down | Every platform UI loses its only login — see [When Authentik is down](<#when-authentik-is-down>) |
| Health check | `kubectl -n authentik get pods,clusters` → server and worker Ready, `authentik-db` healthy |
| UI | `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` |
| Files | `payload/platform/authentik/` |

## Configuration

### Two integration styles

**OIDC**, for applications that can do it themselves: ArgoCD and Grafana map group membership to a role. **Proxy**, for the rest: the hostname resolves to Authentik's embedded outpost, a reverse proxy that authenticates the request and only then forwards it to the backend. It needs nothing from the application and protects exactly as far as nothing else can reach the backend.

```
flowchart LR
    U([Browser]) --> GW[infra-gateway / apps-gateway]
    GW -->|argo, monitoring, OIDC workloads| APP[ArgoCD / Grafana / OIDC workloads]
    APP -.->|OIDC redirect to auth.k8s.wlkr.ch| AK[Authentik]
    GW -->|hubble, rook, prometheus, alertmanager, home, flowscape, analytics, extractor-admin| AK
    AK -->|authenticated| BE[Hubble UI / Ceph dashboard / ...]
```

### One hostname

Authentik answers on `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` only, on `apps-gateway`, which the LAN reaches through the router's local record and the outside through Route53. Every OIDC client and the embedded outpost use that one name.

The outpost is why there is only one. A proxied application's route points at `authentik-server`, but the login itself is an OAuth dance: the outpost sends the browser to the outpost's `authentik_host` to authenticate and gets it back on the application's own hostname. With Authentik on two names and `authentik_host` on the LAN-only one, an application on `apps-gateway` worked at home and redirected outside users to a name that does not resolve. `blueprints.yaml` pins `authentik_host` because the embedded outpost otherwise fills it from `web.base_url` on first start and never updates it.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **A client must never mix names**
>
> The `iss` claim is the hostname the token was issued through. A discovery URI on one name and a redirect on another fails every login with an error that blames the token. Should a second hostname ever come back, pin each client to exactly one.

### Where the proxied routes point

A proxied application's route lives with the application: Hubble's in `payload/platform/cilium/`, Rook's in `payload/platform/rook-ceph/`, Prometheus's and Alertmanager's in `payload/platform/monitoring/`, and Home Assistant's, Flowscape's, Umami's, Wollbi-Fescht's, Wollbi Adventsfenster's and the Extractor admin UI's in the [workloads repository](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/development/add-workload/index.md>), each with `authentik-server` as `backendRef`. Gateway API forbids a cross-namespace `backendRef` unless the target namespace grants it, so `referencegrant.yaml` here allows `HTTPRoute` objects from exactly those namespaces to that Service only. A proxied workload is therefore two pull requests, by design: a workload cannot take itself out from behind the authentication layer on its own.

### Database

`database.yaml` is a CloudNativePG `Cluster` with replicas, the only one on the cluster that has any. Every login on every platform UI goes through Authentik, so its database must survive a node drain: with one instance a reboot kills the database; with replicas, one takes over within a minute, once `enablePDB: false` lets the drain evict the primary. The chart's own Postgres subchart is off — both rules are in [the contract](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/cloudnative-pg/#the-contract>).

The replicas only survive a node loss while they sit on separate nodes, which the operator's own `preferred` anti-affinity does not guarantee — hence the `topologySpreadConstraints` block, under the rule in [Replica placement](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/#replica-placement>).

### Chart values

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `authentik.disable_update_check`, `authentik.disable_startup_analytics` and `authentik.avatars` | Telemetry is switched off in config, not permitted by network policy — the same rule as Grafana, Loki and Alloy. `avatars` only seeds a fresh database: since 2024.2 the setting lives in **System → Settings**, and an existing install keeps calling Gravatar until it is set to `initials` there. Blueprints cannot set it: system settings are an internally managed model, and upstream declined a config-level override in [goauthentik/authentik\#26470](<https://github.com/goauthentik/authentik/issues/26470>) |
| `authentik.web.base_url` | Authentik builds e-mail links and outpost redirects from it and cannot infer it; unset, every admin page shows "The base URL has not been configured". The chart value backfills the tenant, so a rebuilt cluster needs no click |
| `metrics.enabled` and `metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` | The ServiceMonitor renders only when both are set; the switch alone produces nothing, silently. The worker is scraped too: tasks, outpost state and blueprint runs are measured there |
| `postgresql.enabled: false`, `authentik.postgresql.host: authentik-db-rw` and the `global.env` entry | The database is the `Cluster` above. The password is the one CloudNativePG generated into `authentik-db-app`, read as `AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD` from that Secret; it is never copied into OpenBao or Git |
| `server.topologySpreadConstraints` | The chart's `podAntiAffinity` preset is `soft`, which is not enough to hold the replicas apart — see [Replica placement](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/#replica-placement>). The worker is not replicated and needs none |
| `worker.podAnnotations` `homelab.wlkr.ch/secret-generation` | Bumped whenever `authentik-secrets` or a workload's `authentik-secrets-<workload>` gains a key, so ArgoCD restarts the worker in the same sync — see [Pitfalls](<#pitfalls>) |
| Workload blueprints as a `projected` volume, `optional: true` | `blueprints.configMaps` renders a plain `configMap` volume, and the kubelet refuses a pod whose ConfigMap is missing. Workload blueprints arrive with the [workloads](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#workloads-live-in-a-second-repository>), which a fresh cluster may not have yet, so a required mount would keep the worker from starting |

### Where a blueprint lives

Providers and applications are blueprints, so a rebuild reproduces them. `!Find` resolves objects Authentik ships, `!KeyOf` references another entry in the same blueprint, and `!Env` reads an environment variable, which keeps client secrets out of Git. `blueprints_discovery` runs on worker startup, hourly and on a file watcher, asynchronously, so anything configuring itself against a provider must tolerate it not existing yet.

| What | Lives in | Why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform providers, applications, the outpost | `blueprints.yaml` | Mounted into the worker as a ConfigMap |
| A workload's provider and application | The workload's directory in the workloads repository, as the ConfigMap `authentik-blueprint-<application>` targeted at `authentik` | The provider and the application it authenticates change in one commit; the [`authentik-foreign-objects`](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/security-policies/#admission-policies>) policy refuses any other object a workload sends here |
| Client credentials | Generated by a `PushSecret` beside their reader — `secrets.yaml` for the platform's, the workload's own `secrets.yaml` for a workload's — and read here by `secrets-<workload>.yaml` | A workload can mint a pair but not register it: the `ExternalSecret` and mount entry here keep SSO onboarding a deliberate two-repository act |
| The mount entry and `secret-generation` | `application.yaml` | One projected-volume source per workload, with or without credentials; a new credential needs the worker restarted |
| The outpost's `providers:` list | `blueprints.yaml` | It replaces one global object; two repositories writing it would overwrite each other |
| `referencegrant.yaml` | Here | A proxied workload's route needs granting from this side |

### One issuer for OpenCloud

OpenCloud's web, desktop, iOS and Android clients are four OIDC clients with IDs fixed by the clients, so four providers in Authentik, each under an application of its own. The server and the native clients verify every token against one issuer, and Authentik derives a provider's issuer from its application slug, so the four would disagree. All four therefore use `issuer_mode: global`, whose issuer is the bare hostname, and the `HTTPRoute` rewrites `/.well-known/openid-configuration` on that hostname to the `opencloud` application's discovery document, which is where OpenCloud and its clients fetch it. The document names the global issuer and the shared endpoints, so it serves the other three providers as well. Nothing else uses the root path: every other provider is found under its slug.

### User settings flow

Dependency-Track keys its accounts on the `preferred_username` claim, so a user who could rename themselves could take over another's account. `05-user-settings.yaml` therefore gives the default brand its own user settings flow with no username field; a username changes only under **Directory → Users**. It replaces the brand's flow instead of editing the default one because the default blueprint rewrites its own objects on every upgrade, and because the **System → Settings** switch `default_user_change_username` is not a model a blueprint can set.

### Authentication flow

`auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` is reachable from the Internet, and the default authentication flow lets a user without a device in on a password alone. `06-authentication.yaml` gives the default brand its own flow out of the default identification, password and login stages, with two additions. It is an own flow for the same reason as the [user settings flow](<#user-settings-flow>): the default blueprint rewrites its own objects on every upgrade.

| Addition | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Authenticator validation with `not_configured_action: configure`; TOTP and WebAuthn as setup stages, static tokens accepted as a device class | A password alone is one leak away from every application, so a user without a device enrols one at the next login instead of being let through. Static tokens are the recovery codes for a lost phone, enrolled afterwards under **Settings → MFA devices**, which is why they are not offered as the first device |
| A deny stage after identification, selected by a reputation policy on the address and the username with threshold `-5` | Every failed login scores both `-1`, so after five an address or a username is refused for a day (`AUTHENTIK_REPUTATION__EXPIRY`); the password stage's own five-attempt cancel only ends the current attempt. The policy *passes* for a bad score, so it selects a deny stage rather than guarding the flow, and it is evaluated when the stage is reached because the flow's own policies see an anonymous request before the username is known |

To lift a lockout early, delete the score under **Customization → Policies → Reputation scores**.

### Bootstrap credentials

Authentik's built-in bootstrap blueprint creates `akadmin` from `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` only while no `akadmin` exists, and reads nothing from it afterwards. `06-authentication.yaml` then sets the account `is_active: false`: a password-only superuser that never logs in is the one worth guessing, and a disabled one authenticates nowhere. The blueprint touches only `is_active`, so the password and the `authentik Admins` membership stay for break-glass.

Break-glass is `ak shell` from a cluster-admin kubeconfig, which nothing in Authentik can lock out:

```bash
kubectl -n authentik exec deploy/authentik-server -c server -- ak shell -c \
  'from authentik.core.models import User; User.objects.filter(username="akadmin").update(is_active=True)'
```

Then log in with `bootstrap-password` from OpenBao — see [Generated secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#generated-secrets>) — enrol a second factor like any user, and switch the account off again with the same command and `is_active=False`: a blueprint is re-applied only when its file changes, so nothing switches it off for you.

| Variable | Set | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD` | Always, from `bootstrap-password` | Without it a fresh install creates `akadmin` with no usable password, and the initial-setup flow that sets one is open to whoever reaches `auth.k8s.wlkr.ch` first. Blanking it after the first start buys nothing: the account keeps the password |
| `AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` | Never | It mints a non-expiring superuser API token, `authentik-bootstrap-token`, which nothing here uses, and while the variable is set the blueprint recreates the token whenever it is deleted |

A cluster installed before the token was dropped still holds it: delete `authentik-bootstrap-token` under **Directory → Tokens and App passwords**, once the worker has restarted without the variable.

### Groups and roles

Authorisation is group membership. The blueprints create these groups; membership is set by hand under **Directory → Groups**:

| Group | Grants |
| --- | --- |
| `infra-users` | Past the Authentik login of every infra application: ArgoCD, Grafana, Hubble, the Ceph dashboard, Prometheus, Alertmanager, Flowscape and the Extractor admin UI. Grafana `Viewer` for a direct member |
| `argocd-admins` | ArgoCD `role:admin`, and `infra-users` |
| `argocd-viewers` | ArgoCD `role:readonly`, and `infra-users` |
| `grafana-admins` | Grafana `Admin`, and `infra-users` |
| `grafana-editors` | Grafana `Editor`, and `infra-users` |
| `wollbi-editors` | A Payload editor on advent.wollbi.ch and fest.wollbi.ch, created on first sign-in; declared in the two sites' blueprints in the workloads repository |

Every infra application carries a policy binding to `infra-users`, so an account outside it, such as a wollbi editor's, is refused by Authentik before the application sees it. The four role groups have `infra-users` as their parent, and Authentik counts a child group's members as members of the parent. Grafana only sees the groups a user belongs to directly, and with `role_attribute_strict` it refuses a login that matches none of its three. ArgoCD's `policy.default` is empty, so a user in neither ArgoCD group gets **no** access. The wollbi sites bind `wollbi-editors` instead. Home Assistant and Umami have no binding: they have logins of their own.

## Usage

### Client secrets

The OIDC client IDs and secrets are generated once into OpenBao and read by both sides — Authentik through `!Env`, ArgoCD and Grafana through their own `ExternalSecret` — so a rebuilt Authentik gets the same credentials and nothing is copied out of a UI. The `PushSecret` in `secrets.yaml` writes `kv/authentik/config` once — see [Generated secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/#generated-secrets>) — with the secret key, the bootstrap password and the ArgoCD and Grafana client pairs; its `Password` generator's `secretKeys` is the list of keys. A workload's client credentials go in the workload's own path (Dependency-Track's in `kv/dependency-track/config`, each read by its own `secrets-<workload>.yaml`, mounted `optional`): rewriting `kv/authentik/config` would rotate the secret key that signs every session and token, and External Secrets fails an `ExternalSecret` whole when one key is missing, so a shared one would leave a cluster without the workload with no `AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY` either.

The first administrator is created through `akadmin`, switched on for the occasion as in [Bootstrap credentials](<#bootstrap-credentials>); the steps are in [Quickstart step 12](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/#setup>).

### Adding an application

1. Generate its client credentials into OpenBao with a `PushSecret` beside the workload's own `ExternalSecret`, and read them here with an `ExternalSecret` mounted `optional`, like `secrets-dependency-track.yaml`. A public client (PKCE, as OpenCloud's web and native clients) has no credentials: its client IDs are fixed by the client and sit in the blueprint in clear, so this step and step 3 do not apply.
2. Mount the workload's blueprint: in `application.yaml`, a `configMap` source named `authentik-blueprint-<application>` with `optional: true` under `worker.volumes`, in the `projected.sources` of `blueprints-workloads`.
3. Hand the worker the credentials: in the same file, a `secretRef` to `authentik-secrets-<workload>` with `optional: true` under `global.envFrom`, and bump `homelab.wlkr.ch/secret-generation`.
4. Add the provider and application blueprint: an OAuth2 provider with `grant_types`, or a proxy provider added to the outpost's `providers:` list.
5. For a proxied application, point its `HTTPRoute` at `authentik-server`, add its namespace to `referencegrant.yaml`, and add a `toEndpoints` rule for its pods to the `authentik-server` policy in `payload/platform/security/network-policies/authentik.yaml`: the outpost dials the backend, and without the rule the login succeeds and the request after it times out.
6. Bind `infra-users` to an infra application in the blueprint, as an `authentik_policies.policybinding` with the application as `target`. An application with no binding is open to every Authentik account.

### Adding a user

1. Create the account under **Directory → Users**.
2. Add it to `infra-users`, or to a role group from [Groups and roles](<#groups-and-roles>), under **Directory → Groups**. Membership is not blueprinted because that would put a username in the repository, and only a superuser passes the bindings without it.

## Health check

When every login fails, in this order:

1. Server and worker are Ready and the database is healthy:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n authentik get pods,clusters
   ```
2. The discovery document names the one hostname as `issuer`:

   ```bash
   curl -s https://auth.k8s.wlkr.ch/application/o/argocd/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq .issuer
   ```
3. The embedded outpost is healthy (`Outposts` in the admin UI, or):

   ```bash
   kubectl -n authentik logs deploy/authentik-server | grep -i outpost | tail
   ```
4. The worker applied the blueprints — a failed one names its file:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n authentik logs deploy/authentik-worker | grep -i blueprint | tail
   ```

## Pitfalls

> [!CAUTION]
>
> **A new client credential needs the worker restarted**
>
> `envFrom` injects `authentik-secrets` **once, when the pod starts**. A blueprint reading a newly added credential through `!Env` on a running worker gets an empty string and creates a provider that answers 404 on its discovery endpoint. Bumping `secret-generation` restarts the worker in the sync that adds the credential; `kubectl rollout restart` fixes a running cluster but leaves nothing for the next one.

> [!CAUTION]
>
> **A workload blueprint is code with admin rights**
>
> The worker applies a blueprint with full access to Authentik's models, so a blueprint ConfigMap from the workloads repository can create a superuser or add someone to `argocd-admins`. The admission policy limits which ConfigMap a workload may write, not what it says: review a blueprint change in the workloads repository like a change here.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **OAuth2 providers must name their grant types**
>
> `grant_types` defaults to an empty list. A provider that omits it serves no grants, and every login fails with `invalid_request: The request is otherwise malformed`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The outpost entry replaces its provider list**
>
> `authentik_outposts.outpost` sets `providers` wholesale. Every proxied application must be listed there; adding one and forgetting the list silently unassigns the others, which fail open.

> [!NOTE]
>
> **Home Assistant and Umami are the exceptions**
>
> Each has a login of its own and upstream ships no OIDC provider to replace it, so the outpost sits *in front of* it: browser users authenticate twice, which is defence in depth rather than single sign-on. Home Assistant's companion apps and webhooks hold a long-lived token and cannot complete an interactive login, so `skip_path_regex` lets `/api/`, `/auth/token` and the external-auth callback through; Home Assistant's own accounts are the only thing guarding those paths, and revoking an Authentik account does not revoke a Home Assistant token. Umami's tracker script and collect endpoint are loaded by every visitor of every site that embeds it, so `/script.js` and `/api/send` pass the same way; the rest of the dashboard and API stays behind the login.

## Recovery

### When Authentik is down

Single sign-on is a single point of failure for logging in at all. The ArgoCD path needs a working `kubectl`, so keep a kubeconfig off-cluster.

**ArgoCD** — re-enable the local admin account by merging a pull request that sets `admin.enabled` in `payload/argocd/values.yaml`; the `argocd` Application self-heals, so a `kubectl patch` on `argocd-cm` is reverted at the next reconcile. ArgoCD syncs the merge without a login. Then restart the server, which generates `argocd-initial-admin-secret`, and read the password as in [Quickstart](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/quickstart/#setup>). Revert the pull request once Authentik is back.

```bash
kubectl -n argocd rollout restart deploy/argocd-server
```

**Grafana** — the login form is hidden, not removed: the admin account works through the API, and `GF_AUTH_DISABLE_LOGIN_FORM=false` brings the form back.

**Proxied dashboards** have no bypass; port-forward instead:

```bash
kubectl -n kube-system port-forward svc/hubble-ui 8080:80
kubectl -n monitoring port-forward svc/kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus 9090:9090
```

### ArgoCD's API key account

Disabling the local admin also removes its `apiKey` capability. If a token is needed, add an account scoped to what the token is for rather than re-enabling admin:

The `claude` account is one, for the in-cluster agents; see [Agent account](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/argocd/#agent-account>). The shape:

```yaml
configs:
  cm:
    accounts.mcp: apiKey
  rbac:
    policy.csv: |
      p, role:mcp, applications, get, */*, allow
      g, mcp, role:mcp
```

# cert-manager

TLS certificate automation via Let's Encrypt, using DNS-01 challenges through AWS Route53. DNS-01 because these hostnames resolve to RFC1918 addresses that Let's Encrypt cannot reach, and because it is the only way to get a wildcard: one certificate per zone, listed in `payload/platform/certificates/certificates.yaml`, covers every hostname the Gateways terminate.

## At a glance

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Namespace | `cert-manager`; the wildcards land in `kube-system` beside the Gateways, the agent sessions' certificates in their own namespaces; see [SSH listener](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/gateway-api/#ssh-listener>) |
| Depends on | [External Secrets](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/external-secrets/index.md>) for the Route53 credential, so transitively on [OpenBao](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/platform/openbao/index.md>) |
| If it is down | Nothing immediately. Certificates stop renewing, and the consequence surfaces up to sixty days later |
| Health check | `kubectl get certificate -A` → all `READY=True` |
| Files | `payload/platform/cert-manager/`, `payload/platform/certificates/` |

## Configuration

| Setting | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Issuers and certificates in their own `certificates` Application | Kept with cert-manager, the controller would read Degraded until OpenBao held the Route53 credentials — see [Bootstrap convergence](<https://homelab.wlkr.ch/architecture/gitops/#bootstrap-convergence>) |
| Three sync waves inside `certificates`: `ExternalSecret`, then the ClusterIssuers, then the Certificates | In one wave ArgoCD orders custom resources alphabetically — `Certificate`, `ClusterIssuer`, `ExternalSecret`, exactly backwards — and an issuer applied before its Secret stays `Ready=False` with `InvalidSolver` until something resyncs it |
